key_concepts: Stars are huge celestial bodies made of gases that produce light and heat through nuclear
Star color indicates surface temperature, with blue stars hottest and red stars coolest
Stars vary greatly in size and are measured by diameter
Magnitude measures a star's brightness, with lower numbers meaning brighter objects
Apparent magnitude depends on distance, while absolute magnitude or luminosity is intrinsi
Stars form in nebulae and spend most of their lives fusing hydrogen in the main sequence
A star's mass determines its lifetime and death, from white dwarfs to supernovae, neutron
Constellations are groups of visible stars that form patterns when viewed from Earth
Different constellations are noticeable during different seasons of the year
Earth's rotation makes constellations and stars appear to move across the sky
Ancient people used stars and constellations as guides for travel and astronomy
